text: In the Hoare while rule  {I ∧ B} C {I} ⟹ {I} while B do C {I ∧ ¬B},  what is I?
choices: A loop invariant: a predicate re-established by each execution of the body
The negation of the loop guard B
The weakest precondition of the entire program
explanation: I is the loop invariant: true before the loop and preserved by every iteration of body C, so that on exit I ∧ ¬B holds. Choice 1 describes the variant used for termination (total correctness), a separate ingredient; choice 2 is merely ¬B; choice 3 confuses the invariant with wp.
